newsitem.title: INDONESIA: World Bank sees Indonesia C/A deficit $10.1 bln.
newsitem.headline: World Bank sees Indonesia C/A deficit $10.1 bln.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday that Indonesia's current account deficit was likely to reach $10.1 billion, or four percent of gross domestic product (GDP), in the fiscal 1997-98 year (April-March).
The Bank said in its annual report on the Indonesian economy that it expected oil prices to fall back to about $17 per barrel.

"As...investment remains high, import growth will increase the current account deficit. In 1997/98 these developments seem likely to translate into a current account deficit of about $10.1 billion," it said.

"The current acount deficit is likely to remain close to four percent of GDP for the following two years before beginning to fall as a percentage of GDP around the turn of the decade as investments mature," it added.
